name: sec
desc: Event correlation tool for event processing of various kinds
why: Simple Event Correlator is an old-school Perl rule engine for chaining logs and events, a rabbit hole into event processing with a real pedigree.

brief.what_it_is: Simple Event Correlator (SEC) is a lightweight event correlator, per its SourceForge page: a tool for network management, log file monitoring, security management, fraud detection, and other tasks that involve event correlation. It is listed as a non-interactive daemon written in Perl, and the Homebrew formula installs an executable named sec. The homepage did not say in plain words what it takes in or emits, so that detail is unconfirmed. Its scout note describes it as a Perl rule engine for chaining logs and events.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no problem statement beyond the one-line description: event correlation for network management, log monitoring, security and fraud detection.
brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond the Homebrew formula name (sec) was visible on the homepage. The SourceForge listing names Perl as the programming language, so a Perl runtime is implied, but no install steps, configuration, or first-run instructions appeared in what I fetched.
brief.standout: It is an old-school, Perl-based, rule-driven correlator that has been around since at least 2001 (the SourceForge registration date is 2001-12-14), which makes it a historical entry point into event processing. The homepage itself offers little that is distinctive.
brief.status: Probably maintained, but weakly evidenced. SourceForge lists a 'Last Update' of 2026-02-12, which is a download or file date rather than a commit or release date. The listing also shows one user review, rated 5 out of 5. No README or changelog was read to confirm activity.
brief.caveats: The homepage fetch returned mostly SourceForge page chrome, with no README, usage docs, or command examples. I fetched only the homepage and did not follow the optional extra links, so the commands list is empty and how it works is unexplained. The license is GNU GPL version 2.0. The Perl runtime requirement is inferred from the listing, not stated in install docs.
quotes: Simple Event Correlator (SEC) is a lightweight event correlator for network management, log file monitoring, security management, fraud detection, and other tasks which involve event correlation.
fetch_log: https://simple-evcorr.sourceforge.net/ - fetched OK, but the page is SourceForge boilerplate and contains only the project description, license, and metadata; no README or usage docs were present
